record.paper_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
record.original_question: What concrete predictions does branch-cut cosmology make for the primordial energy-density fluctuation spectrum that seeds later structure formation, and can Cosmic Microwave Background measurements from Planck constrain or test those predictions?

evidence.quote: Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) measurements by the Planck satellite Aghanim & et.al. (2020) offer on the other hand an unprecedented opportunity to constrain and test the branch-cut model, particularly regarding the fluctuations associated to the energy density primordial spectrum, the seeds of all structures in the early universe.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the branch-cut cosmology framework, a nonsingular extension of standard Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker cosmology in which the scale factor a(t) is analytically continued onto a Riemann surface so that the cosmological singularity at t = 0 is replaced by a branch cut. Concretely, the usual scale factor a(t) is replaced by a complex-valued function a_β(t) depending on a dimensionless parameter β ∈ (0, 1] such that, in the limit β → 1, one recovers the standard cosmological scale factor, while for β < 1 the function a_β(t) is everywhere nonzero and develops a branch-cut structure that removes the Big Bang singularity. Assuming the usual minimally coupled inflaton-like scalar field dynamics on this analytically extended background, with quantum fluctuations of the energy density propagating on the branch-cut geometry:

(a) Derive an explicit prediction for the primordial scalar power spectrum P_ζ(k) of energy-density fluctuations that seed cosmological structure formation in the branch-cut cosmology, expressed as a function of comoving wavenumber k and of the model parameter β, including its scalar spectral index n_s(β) and any running α_s(β) = dn_s/d ln k.

(b) Determine whether the resulting P_ζ(k), n_s(β), and α_s(β) are compatible with the Cosmic Microwave Background temperature, polarization, and lensing constraints reported by the Planck satellite mission, in particular the measured values of n_s and the upper bound on the tensor-to-scalar ratio r, and identify the range of β (if any) for which the branch-cut prediction is observationally viable.
artifact.status_search_result: Branch-cut cosmology is an active but niche research program, and while subsequent works have begun to compare its predictions with CMB and structure-formation data, a definitive, fully worked-out primordial scalar spectrum with quantitative Planck-based constraints on the model parameter β has not been firmly established in the literature. The question as posed is therefore best characterized as open.

status_evidence.title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists CMB constraints on branch-cut cosmology among open questions for future work.
status_evidence.claim: The authors themselves identify the derivation of the primordial spectrum prediction and its CMB testing as an open question.
